title: Set, Map and JSON
objective: Remove duplicates with Set, keep key-value pairs with Map, copy with spread and turn data into JSON
story: You've docked at a station at the edge of the nebula. The station computer uses a common language to store data and send it to other ships: **JSON**. Today you'll also meet two new boxes called **Set** and **Map**.

sections.title: Set: a box without duplicates
Map: key → value
Spread (...): open and copy
sections.body:
Three dots `...` **open up** an array or object and pour its contents somewhere else. That way you can make copies and combine things:

```js
const crew = ["Ada", "Ben"];
const bigger = [...crew, "Emma"];     // ['Ada', 'Ben', 'Emma']

const ship = { name: "Eagle", fuel: 50 };
const full = { ...ship, fuel: 100 }; // fuel is overwritten
console.log(ship.fuel, full.fuel);   // 50 100
```

Why copy? `const b = a;` doesn't create a new array: `a` and `b` point to the **same** array, so if you change one, the other changes too. `[...a]` gives you a new array.

sections.title: JSON: the common language of data
sections.body:
**JSON** (JavaScript Object Notation) is the standard way to turn data into **text**. Programs use JSON to save data or send it over the internet; data that comes from an API is almost always JSON.

```js
const player = { name: "Ada", level: 3, items: ["shield", "laser"] };

const text = JSON.stringify(player);
console.log(text); // {"name":"Ada","level":3,"items":["shield","laser"]}

const pretty = JSON.stringify(player, null, 2); // indented by 2 spaces, easy to read
const back = JSON.parse(text);                  // an object again from the text
console.log(back.items[1]);                     // laser
```

- `JSON.stringify(data)`: object or array → text. `JSON.stringify(data, null, 2)` splits it into indented lines.
- `JSON.parse(text)`: text → object or array.
- In JSON, keys and text are written in **double quotes**. Functions and `undefined` don't go into JSON.
- If you try to `JSON.parse` broken text, you get a `SyntaxError`.

Later you'll use JSON all the time: when saving with `localStorage` and when getting data from a server with `fetch`.

tasks.title: Unique stars
tasks.prompt:
Some stars were written in the logbook more than once. Use `Set` and spread (`...`) to create a `unique` **array** without duplicates.

Then print `4 different stars` using `unique.length` (don't type the number yourself).
hints: [...new Set(visited)] turns it into an array.

tasks.title: Cargo map
tasks.prompt:
`cargo` is a `Map`. Do the following:

1. Add `"food"` → `15` and `"oxygen"` → `30`.
2. Set the amount of `"water"` to `35`.
3. Add up all the amounts into `total` with `for...of`.
hints: set with the same key updates the value.
for (const [item, amount] of cargo) { total += amount; }

tasks.title: Ship's log
tasks.prompt:
Turn the ship's log into JSON and back:

1. `text`: the JSON text of `log` (`JSON.stringify`).
2. `loaded`: the object turned back from `text` (`JSON.parse`).
3. `nextDay`: a spread copy of `loaded`, but with `day` set to `13`. `loaded` must not change.

challenge.title: Signal counter
challenge.prompt:
Write two functions:

- `countWords(list)`: returns a `Map` holding how many times each word appears (e.g. `"beep"` → `3`).
- `mostCommon(list)`: returns the most common word (you can use `countWords`).
hints: Walk through the Map with for (const [word, count] of ...).
Keep a bestCount variable to find the biggest.

project_task.title: Save file
project_task.prompt:
Prepare the game's save file:

- `saveGame(p)`: takes a copy of the player, removes the **duplicates** in the inventory with `Set` and returns JSON text indented by 2 spaces. The original player object must not change.
- `loadGame(text)`: turns the JSON text back into an object and returns it.
